s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of unilateral arm weakness during a long-haul flight with a background of autoimmune hemolytic anemia
key_facts: 58-year-old woman
Developed right arm weakness 8 hours into a long-haul flight
Medical history of Coombs-positive autoimmune haemolytic anaemia
Presented with dehydration
Blood film showed auto-agglutination with macro-aggregates of red cells
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 119 mm/h
D-dimer was 24.7 nmol/L
Fibrinogen was 15.6 μmol/L
Renal function showed signs of dehydration
Elevated tumor markers
ECG and telemetry showed normal sinus rhythm
Transthoracic echocardiography showed normal cardiac chamber size and function
Brain MRI showed multiple small foci of restricted diffusion
Carotid ultrasound showed normal carotid and vertebral artery anatomy

shortlist.label: Embolic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of unilateral arm weakness and multiple small foci of restricted diffusion on brain MRI

shortlist.label: Antiphospholipid syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: History of autoimmune hemolytic anemia and elevated D-dimer

shortlist.label: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated D-dimer, fibrinogen, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate

shortlist.label: Cancer-associated thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated tumor markers and multiple echogenic targets on echocardiography

shortlist.label: Thrombotic microangiopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia suggested by laboratory results

raw.rationale: The patient's sudden onset of right arm weakness during a long-haul flight, combined with the brain MRI showing multiple small foci of restricted diffusion, suggests an embolic event. The presence of multiple echogenic targets with a snowflake appearance in all four heart chambers on echocardiography further supports this diagnosis.
raw.anchor_refutation: Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria is unlikely as it typically presents with hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and leukopenia, which are not prominently featured in this case. The patient's Coombs-positive autoimmune haemolytic anaemia is a separate condition that does not directly explain the acute neurological symptoms.

rejected.label: Antiphospholipid syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has elevated D-dimer and fibrinogen, there is no clear evidence of antiphospholipid antibodies or a history of recurrent thrombosis.

rejected.label: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
rejected.why: The patient's laboratory results do not show a consistent pattern of consumption coagulopathy, and the clinical presentation is more suggestive of a localized embolic event.

rejected.label: Cancer-associated thrombosis
rejected.why: Although the patient has elevated tumor markers, there is no clear evidence of an active malignancy, and the thrombotic event appears to be more directly related to the embolic source in the heart.

rejected.label: Thrombotic microangiopathy
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and laboratory results do not show the characteristic schistocytes and thrombocytopenia seen in thrombotic microangiopathy.
